newsitem.title: MEXICO: Televisa shares halt slide on board news.
newsitem.headline: Televisa shares halt slide on board news.

text.p: Shares listed by media firm Grupo Televisa SA de CV had pared earlier losses by midday trading on Wednesday on the Mexican bourse but were still weaker on market concerns over a new management line-up.
Televisa CPO shares were down 2.70 pesos at 98.20 pesos, off a mid-morning low of 96.20 pesos, while its ADR was off 1/2 at 25.
"Pressure has eased now we have news of the shareholders' assembly decision regarding the new management," a desk trader said.

Sources close to Televisa told Reuters a shareholders' assembly had named Emilio Azcarraga Jean chairman of the board, while the outgoing chairman, Guillermo Canedo White, was appointed president of the newly created executive commitee.
Azcarraga Jean is the son of Emilio Azcarraga Milmo, a former long standing chairman who died last week. Canedo White is the son of a former close collaborator of Azcarraga Milmo.

"No one likes infighting... Televisa slid yesterday and this morning on newspaper reports Canedo White could be ousted from the board," the trader added. "Nonetheless, we could still see board members scrambling to buy controlling shares."
Traders explained that Televisa listed four share series on the Mexican bourse, the most frequently traded being the CPO series, which carry no voting rights.
The A series has voting rights, but has not been traded since August 9, 1994.
"The A shares are tightly held, but holders of CPOs could, perhaps, come to a deal with a holder of A shares," a trader said.
